allowed_operator_facing_claim: The system successfully interpreted rough conversational instructions during internal development. After identifying that verbatim reproduction created unnecessary presentation and privacy risk, operator-facing records were changed to normalized intent summaries while retaining fingerprint-based audit linkage.

correction_history.correction: Separate robustness evidence from display text; retain normalized intent plus one-way audit binding.
correction_history.discovered_issue: Some operator-facing artifacts reproduced raw typo-bearing wording without adding material audit value.
correction_history.initial_observation: Rough conversational instructions were sufficient to drive bounded internal stages.
correction_history.supported_lesson: Low-friction natural-language control is viable, but operator-facing provenance needs deliberate hygiene.

principles.statement: Execution robustness and presentation hygiene are separate properties.
A rough or typo-bearing instruction may support a bounded robustness claim only when the interpreted scope is independently reviewable.
Operator-facing README files, pull-request bodies, reports, and summaries use normalized intent-preserving wording rather than verbatim raw text.
Audit linkage uses a one-way raw-input fingerprint, normalization actions, and reviewer-confirmed interpreted scope.
The correction history may state that rough-input handling worked and that display hygiene was improved after a presentation risk was discovered.

prohibited_claims: raw errors must be displayed to prove robustness
the raw input can be reconstructed from its fingerprint
purpose: Preserve evidence that the system can interpret rough natural-language instructions without unnecessarily exposing embarrassing, noisy, or privacy-sensitive raw wording in operator-facing artifacts.

forbids: obvious conversion errors presented as user-authored copy
